answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity's action profile is checkpointed per epoch, and the next epoch requires exceeding a similarity threshold against the prior profile; a gale of new accounts all pivoting together fails the match. Genuine agents keep a stable signature, so attackers must run each sybil through slow, costly warm-up epochs that mimic organic drift, and any unity pivot at the nadir of the profile forces restart. Forged copper-thin histories get flagged when variance across epochs collapses. Cost: linear warm-up time per fake identity plus lost epochs on pivot.
